He'd never wanted anyone enough to chase them...until he met her.

Charming, easygoing, and rich beyond belief, Xavier Castillo has the world at his fingertips. 

He also has no interest in taking over his family’s empire (much to his father’s chagrin), but that hasn’t stopped women from throwing themselves at him…unless the woman in question is his publicist. 

Nothing brings him more joy than riling her up, but when a tragedy forces them closer than ever, he must grapple with the uncertainty of his future—and the realization that the only person immune to his charms is the only one he truly wants.  

***
Cool, intelligent, and ambitious, Sloane Kensington is a high-powered publicist who’s used to dealing with difficult clients. 

However, none infuriate—or tempt—her more than a certain billionaire heir, with his stupid dimples and laid-back attitude. 

She may be forced to work with him, but she’ll never fall for him…no matter how fast he makes her heart beat or how thoughtful he is beneath his party persona. 

He’s her client, and that’s all he’ll ever be. Right?

➳ 4.75/5 stars
₊⊹⁀➴ "to every woman who’s ever been told to 'smile more.' fuck that. do what you want.”
First of all, I’m genuinely shocked at how much I loved an Ana Huang book. It’s not that I dislike her, it's just that all her books usually feel the same to me. The characters, the storylines, everything is so predictable. And yes, this one was predictable too, but let me tell you, Ana Huang outdid herself with this one. This book had me giggling and smiling like a teenage girl, and I wasn’t even mad about it!

“Happy? Now you won’t be distracted by my incredible physique.”
“No, I’ll just suffocate beneath the weight of your inflated ego.”


➳ ABOUT THE BOOK

This book revolves around Xavier Castillo, the son of a multi-billionaire who’s carefree, the life of the party, and loves spending his fortune without a second thought. On the flip side, we have Sloane Kensington, a hardworking, responsible, and self-made woman who rebuilt her life after her parents cut her off.

Sloane owns Kensington PR, where Xavier is her client, and let’s just say these two can’t stand each other. She despises his laid-back attitude, and he can’t handle her over-the-top planning. But as they say, opposites attract, and this book is proof of that! Things take a turn when Xavier’s dying father releases a will with a list of rules Xavier has to follow to earn his billion-dollar inheritance. I know, it sounds like a basic plot, but Ana Huang worked her magic with this one. I was so hooked that I finished the book in just two days (though, to be fair, I was on break too).

➳ ABOUT THE CHARACTERS

╰┈➤ XAVIER CASTILLO

Xavier Castillo might just be my favorite Ana Huang man, this guy is literally every girl’s dream. I absolutely loved how deeply he loved Sloane and how he understood her in ways no one else ever did. He has my whole heart, and I completely get why everyone adores him. The way he expressed his emotions, showed incredible mental resilience, and genuinely worked on himself for her was nothing short of swoon-worthy. My man even watched romcoms with her, not because he loved them, but because she did. Bare minimum? Maybe. But the effort was so heart-melting, especially when he remembered little details like her hatred for walnuts and made sure to order food without them.
"I would give anything for her to feel a fraction of the same way toward me."

What truly stood out to me was his journey of growth. He faced his fear of failure head-on, took The Vault seriously, and proved that he could be hardworking and dedicated, not just to win the inheritance but to prove to himself that he could rise to the challenge. And honestly, the way Sloane supported him through it all made their dynamic even more beautiful. She was his rock, his biggest cheerleader, and she did everything to help him reach his full potential. Together, they were just perfection, two opposites bringing out the absolute best in each other.
“She’d obviously dressed with the intention of blending in, but she could no more blend into a crowd than a jewel could blend into mud.”

THIS MAN ISTG 🛐🛐

╰┈➤ SLOANE KENSINGTON

Sloane is me, and I am Sloane. Sloane Kensington, the woman, the myth, the legend. Honestly, she might be the sole reason I rated this book so highly! If you know me, you know I’m a sucker for a strong fmc, and Sloane was everything I could ever hope for and more. Not gonna lie, my expectations for her were pretty low at first because she was always portrayed as shy and quiet in the other books. I was intrigued, sure, but I fully expected another spineless fmc that would just piss me off. But nope, Sloane completely shattered my expectations and claimed her throne as my new favorite Ana Huang heroine. Sorry, Jules, but you’ve been officially dethroned.

What I loved most about Sloane was her emotional strength and resilience. She was considered icy by so many people, but let’s be real, how could someone be icy when they’d go out of their way to love and care for their stepsister, Penelope? Or feel completely heartbroken over the death of a pet fish? Sure, she was emotionally reserved, but that didn’t make her cold or unlovable. People also called her rude, and honestly, can you blame her? Her fiancé cheated on her with her own sister, Georgia, who had the audacity to flex that she was “the first choice.” Like, seriously, what is wrong with you, Georgia?
“I cared. More than cared. He made me feel everything when I’d thought I could feel nothing, and that realization led to an undeniable truth: I loved him, so much so that I couldn’t breathe, and I’d pushed him away because I knew love would only end in heartbreak.”

Anyways, Sloane was a queen through and through. Hardworking, dedicated, sassy, and unapologetically badass, she was everything I love in an FMC. Yes, she was a little closed off, but not everyone is a bubbly, smiley ball of sunshine all the time, and that’s okay. Let’s normalize being true to ourselves, even if that means setting boundaries and not taking anyone’s crap. Sloane was unapologetically herself, and I adored every single page she was on.
"But he wasn’t a random man; he was him, and the house felt so much more vibrant when he was there that I’d thrown caution to the wind and invited him over for the weekend."


➳ FINAL THOUGHTS

I went into this book with very low expectations, especially after not enjoying the last two books in the series. But let me tell you, Ana Huang absolutely outdid herself with this one, and I mean that from the bottom of my heart. The writing felt so smooth and effortless, making it such an easy and enjoyable read. Honestly, I ended up loving it way more than I ever thought I would. Xavier and Sloane? Literal perfection. They’ve officially claimed the top spot as my favorite Ana Huang couple ever.
"Now we lived together in a townhouse with a pet fish and a rooftop movie theater, and we were nauseatingly, disgustingly blissful."

What really stood out to me was how this book just had that vibe, it was fun, charming, and so full of heart that I couldn’t stop smiling. The banter, the chemistry, the emotional growth, it all came together beautifully. The story felt light and engaging, yet it had enough depth to keep me hooked from start to finish.

⚘ "Overall, if you’re in the mood for a book that’ll light up your face and make you giggle like a teenager crushing on their favorite fictional couple, this one is the perfect catch for you. Trust me, you’re going to have a blast with it!" 💌

4.25 stars

“I loved seeing her like this. Wild, uninhibited, and so damn beautiful that it made my heart ache.”


Finally, a good book in the KOS series! Honestly, I kind of gave up on this series after KOG, but Ana really surprised me with this book and Xavier and Sloane’s story. This book is totally different from what she usually writes, and I love how she’s experimenting with different characters and stories—ones that aren’t solely focused on romance but also on character growth and development. The storyline revolves around two things—Xavier and his new business venture, and their trial dating period. And somewhere in between, their attraction blossomed into love and something more.

“Just shut up and follow me,” I snapped, wishing I had a wittier reply.
“Yes, ma’am.” His cheeks dimpled. “I love a woman in charge.”


Sloane Kensington is independent, responsible, and intelligent. She’s the woman everyone fears—cool and composed, never overreacting in any situation. Except when it comes to Xavier. He made her go bonkers with his antics, lol. She hides behind the façade of an ice queen because it protects her from potential hurt, and her fears were justified—her ex was an absolute asshole, and both he and her family gave her serious trust issues. People said she didn’t feel emotions or care, but Sloane felt everything—she just didn’t express it like others. She needed someone who would love and accept her for who she was, and Xavier did exactly that. I loved how she didn’t hold herself back when he asked her to go on a trip, how he challenged her, pushed her out of her comfort zone, yet always made sure she felt safe. She was also giving me Jules vibes with her comebacks.

“You think you know me so well,” I whispered, even though he was right.
“Only parts of you.” The gentle brush of his thumb against my hand unlocked a colony of butterflies in my stomach. “But we’ll get there.”


Xavier Castillo is the epitome of a shameless flirt and effortless charm. But beneath all that is a man with raw vulnerability, scarred by his father’s treatment. I get why he was so stubborn and inconsiderate all these years, and I’m proud of him for finding his passion and working hard to make it a reality. He’s thoughtful and caring, and I love how much he paid attention to Sloane, he noticed everything about her. He’s so observant and stubborn when it comes to her. I fell for him in the very first chapter despite him being a playboy, and I liked that he wasn’t sexualising her every other moment like men in books usually do. Not once did he obsess over other women—Sloane was the only one who made him crazy and delusional. He’s so unhinged sometimes, always bribing people just to get to Sloane faster, but he’s also the sweetest, craziest person ever. The dates and outings he planned for her had me swooning so hard! He’s one of the best MMCs Ana has written and my favourite KOS series man. Period.

“You would rather watch a rom-com about a witch and a plumber falling in love than attend a costume party with celebrities?”
“One hundred percent. As long as I’m watching it with you.”


Xavier and Sloane are absolute perfection. The romance was executed so perfectly—it wasn’t insta-love or insta-lust. It was about getting to know each other, giving a chance to the attraction that had been simmering between them for three years, slowly warming up to each other, breaking down the barriers they had built around their hearts, and falling in love in the process. It was simple, cute, and beautiful. Xavier and Sloane have opposite personalities, yet in some ways, they share the same fears and insecurities. Both were deprived of love and affection by their parents, but they loved each other with their flaws, not despite them. The way Xavier encouraged Sloane to step outside her comfort zone, and how she supported him at every step of his new business venture, was so endearing.

“I don’t want a kiss or a one-night stand,” he said. “I want you. I want to know you outside work. I want to take you on real dates. And I don’t know if it’ll work out in the end, but I want us to at least try.”


The ice queen x sunshine trope was executed so well. I loved their trips, their witty banter, the sexual tension, the dates Xavier planned (which were everything a girl deserves from a man), the effort they put into understanding each other, how they truly listened to each other’s stories, and their love confessions. Xavier and Sloane are the softest couple Ana Huang has ever written.

“I needed her the way the ocean tides needed the moon, and I would give anything for her to feel a fraction of the same way toward me.”


I loved Ana’s writing in this one; she included so many cameos from previous books, and my heart was full of happiness and nostalgia. This book also has some of the best love declarations at the end, and as unrealistic and dreamy as they were, my romantic heart loved every second of it. I loved how raw and relatable the characters were, watching them grow and step outside their comfort zones.

The ending was the cutest! I seriously cried because I was so happy for these two idiot dorks. The third-act breakup was unnecessary as always—it’s Ana, so she had to throw it in. I would’ve loved for the mystery behind The Vault’s fire to be explained, but maybe it was left open for a future book.

I really can’t wait for Ayana and Vuk’s book! I have a thing for broken, tortured heroes, so I already know I’m going to love it.

“Love isn’t about perfection, Luna; it’s about imperfect people creating their own version of happily ever after.”

I am not going to write a detailed review for this because I honestly don't have much to say. This was better than pride and greed but not as good as wrath. I don't know how to describe this but writing style for KOW and KOG was very easy to read and had you entertained but for this and pride it wasn't like that I often found myself getting bored but the characters and the plot actually kept up so I did not mind it that much. I had problems but I still enjoyed it.

Xavier was amazing to read and Sloane was so different maybe that why I liked her so much, I also loved how we explored a lot of their past which made me like their characters a lot and they also didn't do anything to frustrate you so that was a plus. Sloane's relationship with Pen was so cute and Xavier going out of his way to arrange meeting between them was also so wholesome. I also liked how Xavier paid attention to Sloane and learned everything about her. I liked the moments between them but I wasn't in love with them and the spice (I cant believe im saying this) wasn't that spicy.

This book was easily the most plotty. There were some moments that were just so good especially that will scene. I was more happy with the plot than I was with the romance because I wanted to see what happens and how Xavier might handle things, was also intrigued by the vault and the mysteries revolving around it which was all just so interesting. Also that one interaction b/w Xavier and his Aunt, AHH I have never been more satisfied.

We got cameos of Alex, All the KOS girls, Kai and mentions of Jules, Bridget, Rhys, Ava, Christian and Dante I might be missing some...so this was filled with it and I think moving forward in terms of plot there will definitely be more of these Cameos and honestly I enjoyed them.

Overall in terms of plot and characters I would say this book was a solid 4 but it didnt quite deliver on the romance aspect as much as I was expecting it to so I had to lower my rating. The series is improving a lot tho and I am very excited for book 5!

❝ whenever i was drowning, she was my anchor in the storm. ❞


‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ just when i had officially given up on this series and was rotting in the ninth circle of romance hell, screaming "no more billionaire trauma dumps," ana guang yeeted king of sloth at my skull like a divine intervention and said "here, you ungrateful little raccoon, eat this." (she didn't actually say that but the vibes were there). after dragging my corpse through king of pride and king of greed (which felt like emotional waterboarding), i swore i was done. finished. retired from rich people feelings. but then the reverse sunshine trope whispered my name and my clown nose slid right back on like the weak, predictable gremlin i am.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ i. plot and characters. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ sloane kensington is a publicist who could ruin your entire bloodline before her morning oat milk latte. to her elite clients she's a terrifying ice queen in a pencil skirt who weaponizes competence like it's a tactical nuke. but underneath that glacial resting bitch face is a very tired, very squishy woman who just wants to not be disappointed for once in her goddamn life. her armor is thick, her insecurities are loud, and when she goes feral? chef's kiss. i respect a girl who can be protective, petty, and ready to throw hands while still looking immaculate.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ xavier castillo is marketed as an international walking scandal and billionaire playboy, but on-page he's actually a dangerously observant, stupidly thoughtful golden retriever in human form. this man was in his emo "i don't care about anything" era, yet he was out here memorizing sloane's coffee order, tracking her micro-expressions like it was his full-time job, and cataloging her moods with the dedication of a man who has never heard of google calendar. i can't even get a situationship to remember my birthday without a formal evite and xavier is over here treating sloane's preferences like sacred scripture. be so fucking serious right now.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ and the cameos? delightful. all the previous rich traumatized idiots running around living their little happily-ever-afters like it's a billionaire reunion special. good for them. i'm happy for my silly little universe of walking red-flag collections.


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ ii. romance. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ this is reverse sunshine executed so perfectly i was straight-up feasting like a raccoon in a dumpster behind a five-star restaurant. grumpy ice-queen girl meets golden-retriever sunshine boy and i lost my entire mind. the romance is deliciously sloooow in the best way. they're learning each other's tells, picking up tiny details, and lowering their walls one molecule at a time like two emotionally constipated people who finally found someone worth the therapy bill.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ therre's no cheap trauma-dump bonding here. just two disasters actually getting to know each other while the plot gets gritty with heavier themes and messier backstories. it gave them texture, depth, and enough emotional baggage for a therapist to retire comfortably on. their connection actually felt earned instead of slapped on.

─〝 every version of my happily ever after will always include some version of you. 〞


₊˚꒰ 𖧷 ꒱ ⊹ iii. conclusion. ₊˚⊹ ꒱
‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ this book turned me into a giggling, feral mess more than once. i genuinely enjoyed it, against my will and better judgment. the longer length actually slapped for me; the extra page time gave space for the slow build, deeper character work, and maximum time to watch xavier be an absolute unhinged menace with a heart of gold.

‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ does it dethrone king of wrath for me? absolutely not. dante is still my number one husband, the love of my life, and i will ride or die on this hill with zero notes and a baseball bat. but xavier definitely joined the ana huang men™ lineup in my brain and set up permanent residence. i can have multiple billionaire obsessions, actually. it’s called range. polyamory for fictional men is valid. and yes, i will continue letting this series emotionally whiplash me into next year because apparently i enjoy pain, bad decisions, and learning absolutely nothing.

— 3.5 stars. ⋆˚☆˖°

1.5 ☆
“Whenever I was drowning, she was my anchor in the storm.”
I read this in one sitting because I knew I would not pick it back up if I put it down. This did not need to be over 450 pages.

Pros
• I enjoyed seeing and hearing about so many characters from the author's different books.

Cons
• I didn't expect so much family drama. I can't stand family drama, especially if at some point some of the crappy family is forgiven in a way. (SLIGHT SPOILER) Like in the epilogue, it said she was doing therapy with them. And the drama just felt unnecessary. I found myself rolling my eyes and getting so annoyed at the fmc’s family.
• The characters got together way too soon considering how long the book was. I felt like there was not enough build-up. It just kind of happened.
• I didn't like the mmc at all. I don't understand how a grown man, about to hit 30 years old, acts like a brat and parties and sleeps around so much. I don't find it attractive. And I get he had “character growth”, but I am so over the “I was a playboy but then I screw you” trope. I can’t even say “but then I met you” in this situation. ⇩
• They have worked together for around 3 years and the fmc has had to clean up his messes with the public and had to deal with his attitudes. I get that he has trauma and daddy issues, but I am so tired of it. It just isn't an excuse anymore in my opinion.
• The fmc was labelled as “ice queen” and “cold”, but I just feel like she wasn't. I didn't get that vibe. I felt like sometimes she let certain people in her family walk all over her in a way. I get she had the last “laugh”, but there were so many situations where I wanted her to leave the situation or punch someone. I felt like we were told she was someone who didn't “feel”, but every chapter was saying how she did feel and how sad or tired she was about stuff. Considering the fmc “doesn't cry” she sure had a lot of moments where she was about to.

Upcoming books in the series
I do plan on reading the rest of the series. I am very excited about the next book with Vuk😚. But I am worried the quality is decreasing with this series😬.

The pacing is deliberate, almost languid... but beneath all that calm surface, there lies a storm of emotions. Xavier's slowness isn’t laziness- it’s fear, hesitation, the weight of unspoken feelings. Watching him peel back those layers one by one was both frustrating and achingly tender for me.
His hesitation, his fear, his slow unraveling- it all made me cry more times than I care to admit. And Sloane? She is the emotional Swiss Army knife of the KoS universe. She can fix a scandal, a broken heart and probably your taxes, all while looking devastatingly good in a simple black gown!!

He thought, "... her skin glowed like pearls kissed by moonlight."

AHHH ♡♡♡

My gaze skimmed over her quickly enough to escape her notice, yet long enough to imprint the image in my mind. On anyone else, her simple black gown would’ve been boring, but Sloane could wear a grocery bag and still blow everyone else out of the water.

Nothing brightened my day more than riling Sloane up.

Odds were, she was picturing stabbing me with it, but I didn’t mind a little hypothetical violence. It kept things interesting. LOL

Ahhh! Stop making me blush, Xavier!

AND SLOANE IS THE ONLY WOMAN IN ANA HUANG'S UNIVERSE THAT IS SO ME-CODED!

Overall, I loved this one.
Xavier Castillo: rich, ridiculously good looking and allergic to responsibility.
Sloane Kensington: a workaholic who treats incompetence like a personal insult.
